Subject: Acme - Rerank model validation (NDCG/MRR) & next steps

Hi Alex / Maria

Great to meet you on the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Recap (5-min):
- Goal: improve top-K search relevance on product search results (focus: homepage + category pages).
- Current signal: Acme has clickstream + human-labeled relevance for ~75k queries.
- Priority metrics: NDCG@5 (primary), MRR (secondary), latency target <= 60ms P95 for rerank tier.

Recommended initial model candidates for validation:
- redwood/rerank-v1 (quantized 8-bit): high throughput, optimized for sparse vectors + pairwise rerank.
- roberta-large-similarity (fp16): strong semantic understanding for ambiguous queries.
- baseline: current in-prod logistic-rerank model (for delta comparison).

What we need from you:
1) Share a sample eval set (CSV/JSONL) with query, candidate list, and labels (even a 5k sample is sufficient for an initial validation).
2) Confirm SLA constraints for pilot (latency + cost per 1M requests).

What we'll deliver (next 7 business days):
- NDCG@1/3/5 and MRR results for the three model candidates (attached: acme_rerank_eval_ndcg_mrr.xlsx).
- A recommended A/B plan with traffic split and rollback criteria (attached: acme_rerank_ab_plan.pdf).
- Prompt/prefix set and the exact scoring prompt we used (attached: prompt_set_v2.jsonl).

Proposed timeline:
- Today/Tomorrow: you share sample eval data / grant Drive access.
- Wed: Redwood runs evals and shares preliminary NDCG/MRR.
- Fri: Review A/B plan and schedule a 30-minute sync with your infra/engineering to confirm rollout.

Attachments: acme_rerank_eval_ndcg_mrr.xlsx, prompt_set_v2.jsonl, acme_rerank_ab_plan.pdf

Thanks — excited to help get the rerank lift quantified.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Alex - quick answers inline and next steps: 

- Eval sample: great, once the Drive link is live I'll pull it and run the 10k through our offline harness.
- Latency: redwood/rerank-v1 in a two-GPU pilot with continuous batching typically hits P95 ~45-55ms for 20-token average candidate scoring (we'll send precise numbers; depends on batch sizing). roberta-large-similarity is closer to 70-90ms P95 (higher quality on ambiguous queries but costlier).
- Cost: estimated unit cost for redwood/rerank-v1 in pilot config: ~$65 per 1M reranks (includes infra + model execution) - we'll produce a cost breakdown.
- Ownership: Rishi (cc'd) will own the A/B playbook and rollout automation; Vivek will be the engineering contact for infra/latency tuning.

Plan for this afternoon: I'll run the initial eval and upload the NDCG/MRR workbook (attached). Summary of preliminary results (offline 10k sample):
- redwood/rerank-v1: NDCG@5 = 0.481, MRR = 0.389 (relative +12% NDCG vs baseline)
- roberta-large-similarity: NDCG@5 = 0.493, MRR = 0.402 (relative +15% NDCG vs baseline)
- baseline (logistic): NDCG@5 = 0.428, MRR = 0.339

Notes: roberta-large shows slightly better quality but doubles cost and increases latency risk. Recommended approach: pilot with redwood/rerank-v1 as the canary and run a small traffic slice (10%) to roberta-large for quality comparison.

Attachments: acme_rerank_eval_ndcg_mrr.xlsx (contains full metric table and per-query deltas)

Internal notes / recommended A/B config (cc: Marissa who is coordinating externally):

- A/B design: start with 5% traffic to redwood/rerank-v1 vs 95% baseline for initial monitoring (48 hours). If no regression in CTR and NDCG@5 uplift > 8% and latency SLO met, ramp to 25% for 72 hours, then 50% if stable.
- Canary: include user-segment guardrails (only US desktop traffic) and throttle back if P95 > 65ms or relative drop in CTR > 2%.
- Rollback automation: set Alert rule in Console: if latency P95 > 65ms or NDCG@5 drops below baseline for 3 consecutive 1-hour windows -> automatic rollback to baseline model and page-level serve.
- Metrics to capture: NDCG@1/3/5, MRR, CTR, latency P50/P95, cost per 1M.
- Cost/backstop: estimate incremental infra cost for 25% traffic ~ $2.4k/day (pilot estimate) - share exact calc in shared Drive.

I uploaded a short runbook for automated rollback and metric thresholds to: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AcmeRerankEvals (see "playbooks/runbook-rerank-rollback.md").

I'll be available for the Wed infra sync to help configure tracing and tracing hooks for per-token breakdowns.

Rishi
